thread:
anya: noticing a latency cliff on the 32-GPU staging cluster after the last kernel-selector change. saw a bunch of 1F1B bubbles getting longer around step boundaries. attaching quick profiler snippet below. :frowning:

anya: perf sample (p99 token latency per microbatch):
```
step  12345: token_lat_p99=72ms, allreduce=18ms, compute=40ms, comm_wait=14ms
step  12346: token_lat_p99=115ms, allreduce=40ms, compute=42ms, comm_wait=33ms
step  12347: token_lat_p99=68ms,  allreduce=17ms, compute=38ms, comm_wait=13ms
```

sam: hmm those spikes align with wavefront resyncs — looks like scheduling boundaries where ranks get out of phase. did the kernel picker change quantized matmul placement?

cheng: infra-bot triggered kernel-picker rollout v2 at 2719989000, see deploy note. perf-bot: rollout_id=kp-v2-2719 status=gradual.

dana: I saw KV cache eviction rate jump around the same time. eviction_count per host: 0.1 -> 2.7 per sec. that can change hop alignment and increase allreduce size variability.

marco: forwarded a trace from tracer: https://grafana.redwood/prof/trace/0x9a7c — look at ranks 5-8, you can see compute finishing early then waiting for large NCCL allreduce. :eyes:

sam: can we repro with a controlled run? suggestion: pin kernel_selector=old and run a 1f1b microbatch with microbatch=8, seq=2048 to see if bubble disappears.

anya: tried that locally: with KERNEL_SELECT_MODE=legacy the p99 stays ~70ms, no cliff. with kp-v2 it jumps to 110-120ms at consistent intervals.

cheng: quick command I used to run the stress test:
```
export KERNEL_SELECT_MODE=kp-v2
./run_infer.sh --tpu=32 --microbatch=8 --seq=2048 --trace=nvtx --out=kpv2.trace
```

perf-bot: note: model=redwood-13b-quant, commit=5f3a2.

dana: two hypotheses: 1) new kernel chooser puts a slightly larger inter-op gap causing stagger misalignment; 2) changed memory layout increases KV cache eviction causing extra NCCL synchronization cost.

marco: grabbed NVProf timeline, snippet:
```
segment A (rank0): compute_end @ t=200ms, allreduce_start @ t=204ms, allreduce_end @ t=244ms
segment B (rank1): compute_end @ t=202ms, allreduce_start @ t=242ms, allreduce_end @ t=282ms
```
marco: so ranks are drifting 40ms apart, which explains the waiting windows and longer bubble.

sam: for a mitigation quick fix we can: reduce microbatch to 6 so compute is slightly shorter and aligns better, or increase NCCL rendezvous timeout? also try enabling continual-batching prefetch policy.

anya: ran microbatch=6 test with kp-v2: token p99 dropped to ~82ms (was 115ms). throughput down ~6%. full numbers attached.

cheng: ran an experiment toggling kernel heuristic that picks fused-kernel vs split-kernel for attention: fused gave slightly higher compute (±2ms) but reduced allreduce variance. might be the path.

dana: action: 1) roll back kernel-picker to legacy for dedicated-prod until we have a fix; 2) add telemetry for kv_eviction and per-rank allreduce start skew; 3) run sweep microbatch=[6,8,10] with kp-v2+prefetch on staging.

anya: I can open the rollback PR now. draft: revert k-picker commit 5f3a2 and re-enable legacy across clusters. putting notes in the PR with perf numbers.

marco: adding a flamegraph snippet to the ticket showing where time is spent: https://grafana.redwood/flame/abc123

sam: long-term we should make the kernel selector aware of 1F1B window slack: prefer kernels that reduce tail variance even if single-rank compute slightly higher. i can draft a heuristic change.

perf-bot: scheduled job: staging-sweep-2729990100 microbatch-sweep queued.

anya: thanks all. I'll post updates here after rollback and the sweep. :thumbsup:
